title: Editing Driver Character: Socially-Controllable Behavior Generation for Interactive Traffic Simulation

control_signal.value: A scalar courtesy level for the simulated agent, defined as the change in the other agent's expected reward caused by its trajectory; users give it as a quantile in the unit interval.

control_mechanism.value: Courtesy coefficient is an input to the trajectory generator; training uses auto-labeled courtesy values, data augmentation with predicted trajectories, and a differentiable courtesy loss. A range predictor normalizes values per scenario.

base_model.value: Multipath++ backbone (scene encoder, multi-context gating decoder) with anchor embeddings removed to output a single-modal trajectory; decoder trained on a pretrained encoder.

datasets.value: Waymo Open Motion Dataset, interactive subset with labeled pairs of interacting agents.

metrics.value: CourtesyMSE (controllability) and TrajADE against ground truth (realism); predictor ADE, minADE, minFDE, MR, mAP; correlation between input quantile and generated courtesy.

controllability_evidence.value: Full model reaches CourtesyMSE 0.120 with range-predicted values; generated courtesy correlates with input quantile at 0.60 on the full interactive validation subset and 0.79 on the high-courtesy subset.

stated_limitations.value: Auto-labeling is affected by the causality issue of conditional behavior prediction, which cannot separate correlation from causation between two agents' trajectories; single-modal output; closed-loop extension is future work.

notes: Single-agent open-loop trajectory generation; closed-loop use is stated as future work.
